parole.significato: A wooden-keyed percussion idiophone of West Africa that is struck with two padded sticks.
The currency of the Gambia, divided into 100 bututs.
A member of the Mandinka people.
parole.testo: From Mandinka Mandinka. Compare French mandingue, from the same source.

parole.significato: A member of a particular people of West Africa.
parole.testo: From Mandinka Mandinka (“someone from Mande”), from Mandiŋ (“Mande”) + -ka (“inhabitant suffix”).

parole.significato: A deity or other supernatural being said to have been worshipped by certain West African peoples; an idol.
parole.testo: Probably from Mandinka maamajomboo (“mask; masked dancer”); or perhaps from /l/-vocalization in the words mumble and jumble.

parole.significato: A West African talisman or charm.
A stringed musical instrument (chordophone), usually with a round body, a membrane-like soundboard and a fretted neck,…
parole.testo: From the pronunciation of African slaves, of unknown ultimate origin. Possibly a corruption of bandore (from Spanish bandurria), alternatively from a West African language such as Mandinka banjul, or Kimbundu mbanza.
